beats.text: The villain is anatomical fragmentation. Every robot chassis speaks a different motor language, forcing engineers to rebuild policies from scratch.
beats.visual_focus: Multiple robot arms with mismatched joint coordinate systems.

beats.text: GreenWAM shatters this by mapping twenty robot families into one shared anatomical action space using common joint coordinates.
beats.visual_focus: Normalization of diverse robot joints into a single coordinate grid.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—I've definitely seen robots fail at simple tasks because of hardware differences, so that hit home. I like that you didn't use 'smart robot brains' or other cringe metaphors. My only hang-up is 'shared anatomical action space'; it sounds a bit like a buzzword salad. I get the gist that you're normalizing coordinates, but that specific phrase felt like it was trying too hard to sound academic.

thriller_metadata.physical_analogy: A Tower of Babel where every robot speaks a different motor dialect, forcing engineers to rebuild policies from scratch for every chassis.
thriller_metadata.paradigm_shift: One foundation model mastering diverse robot bodies through unified latent representation.
